title: Organic Chemistry
seo_title: Secondary 4 Chemistry: Organic Chemistry Worksheets (O-Level 6092 with Answers)
standard_text: Describe crude oil as a mixture of hydrocarbons separated by fractional distillation and state the uses of its fractions; describe cracking; describe a homologous series and state the general formulae and functional groups of alkanes, alkenes, alcohols and carboxylic acids; draw and name structural isomers; describe combustion and substitution of alkanes, addition reactions of alkenes with bromine, hydrogen and steam, the manufacture of ethanol, oxidation of ethanol and the formation of esters; describe addition and condensation polymerisation and the problems of disposing of plastics (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Chemistry 6092 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Chemistry worksheets on organic chemistry: crude oil, cracking, alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids, esters, isomers and polymers. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ, alcohols –OH, acids –COOH.
body_html:
How to think about it

Count the carbons for the name; find the functional group for the reactions.

  • meth- 1, eth- 2, prop- 3, but- 4, pent- 5. Alkanes -ane, alkenes -ene, alcohols -anol, acids -anoic acid (the –COOH carbon counts).
  • Alkenes add bromine (decolourised), hydrogen (Ni) and steam (H₃PO₄) across C=C. Alkanes only burn or substitute in UV light.
  • Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid; acid + alcohol → ester + water (alcohol part first: ethyl ethanoate).
  • Addition polymers come from C=C monomers with no other product; condensation polymers (nylon, PET) also give water.
Example

Name the ester from propanoic acid and methanol.

alcohol part first: methyl

acid part: propanoate

Answer: methyl propanoate

Example

Formula of butene?

alkene CₙH₂ₙ, n = 4

Answer: C₄H₈

Common mistakes

  • Using CₙH₂ₙ for alkanes.
  • Naming esters with the acid first.
  • Forgetting the –COOH carbon (C₂H₅COOH is propanoic acid).
  • Saying alkanes decolourise bromine water.
  • Saying addition polymers give water.

faq.q: How do you name an ester?
faq.a: The alcohol gives the first word ending in -yl and the acid gives the second word ending in -anoate: ethanol + propanoic acid gives ethyl propanoate.

faq.q: What is the difference between addition and condensation polymers?
faq.a: Addition polymers form from monomers with C=C bonds and nothing else is made. Condensation polymers form from monomers with two functional groups and a small molecule such as water is lost each time.

faq.q: What is the test for an alkene?
faq.a: Shake with bromine water: an alkene turns it from orange to colourless; an alkane leaves it orange.

items.q: Cracking: C₈H₁₈ → C₃H₈ + ?. What is the missing product?
items.e: Atoms are conserved: C8 − C3 = C5, H18 − H8 = H10 (an alkene).

items.q: One molecule of an alkane with 8 carbon atoms (C₈H₁₈) burns completely. How many molecules of water are made?
items.e: Carbon → CO₂ (8), hydrogen → H₂O (9).

items.q: Where in the fractionating column do the fractions with the lowest boiling points come out?
items.e: The column is coolest at the top.

items.q: One molecule of ethane (C₂H₆) burns completely. How many molecules of carbon dioxide are made?
items.e: Carbon → CO₂ (2), hydrogen → H₂O (3).

items.q: Cracking: C₁₀H₂₂ → C₅H₁₂ + ?. What is the missing product?
items.e: Atoms are conserved: C10 − C5 = C5, H22 − H12 = H10 (an alkene).

items.q: Which fraction of crude oil is used for fuel for lorries and trains?
items.e: Bitumen has the longest chains; refinery gases the shortest.

items.q: One molecule of pentane (C₅H₁₂) burns completely. How many molecules of carbon dioxide are made?
items.e: Carbon → CO₂ (5), hydrogen → H₂O (6).

items.q: Which fraction of crude oil is used for fuel for ships and power stations?
items.e: Bitumen has the longest chains; refinery gases the shortest.

items.q: Cracking: C₁₆H₃₄ → ? + C₂H₄ (ethene). What is the missing product?
items.e: Atoms are conserved: the other product is an alkane, C14H30.

items.q: What is a homologous series?
c: a family of compounds with the same general formula and functional group, and similar chemical properties
compounds made from the same element
compounds with the same boiling point
compounds with the same molecular formula
items.e: Physical properties change gradually down the series.

items.q: Which fraction of crude oil is used for bottled gas for heating and cooking?
items.e: Bitumen has the longest chains; refinery gases the shortest.

items.q: Cracking: C₈H₁₈ → ? + C₄H₈ (butene). What is the missing product?
items.e: Atoms are conserved: the other product is an alkane, C4H10.

items.q: One molecule of methane (CH₄) burns completely. How many molecules of water are made?
items.e: Carbon → CO₂ (1), hydrogen → H₂O (2).

items.q: Which fraction of crude oil is used for fuel for aircraft?
items.e: Bitumen has the longest chains; refinery gases the shortest.

items.q: Which fraction of crude oil is used for fuel for cars?
items.e: Bitumen has the longest chains; refinery gases the shortest.

items.q: One molecule of ethane (C₂H₆) burns completely. How many molecules of water are made?
items.e: Carbon → CO₂ (2), hydrogen → H₂O (3).

items.q: How is crude oil separated into fractions?
items.e: Fractions with different boiling points condense at different heights in the column.

items.q: One molecule of pentane (C₅H₁₂) burns completely. How many molecules of water are made?
items.e: Carbon → CO₂ (5), hydrogen → H₂O (6).

items.q: What is the main use of ethanol made by fermentation?
c: as a fuel and in alcoholic drinks
items.e: It is renewable because sugar comes from plants.

items.q: What is petrol used for?
items.e: Each fraction has molecules of similar chain length.

items.q: An alkane has 12 carbon atoms. How many hydrogen atoms does it have?
What is the general formula of the alkanes?
items.e: Each member differs from the next by CH₂.

items.q: How many structural isomers are there of butene, C₄H₈ (straight and branched alkenes)?
items.e: Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (a different chain or position of the functional group).

items.q: Which compound has the formula C₂H₆?
items.e: Count the carbon atoms (2: eth-) and look at the functional group.

items.q: What is the functional group of the carboxylic acids?
items.e: The functional group decides the chemical reactions of the series.

items.q: Which alkane has the formula C₅H₁₂?
items.e: Meth 1, eth 2, prop 3, but 4, pent 5, hex 6.

items.q: What is the functional group of the alkenes?
items.e: The functional group decides the chemical reactions of the series.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of butanoic acid?
items.e: Butanoic acid has 4 carbon atoms (but-). Carboxylic acids are CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH, and the carbon in –COOH is counted in the name.

items.q: How many structural isomers are there of butane, C₄H₁₀?
items.e: Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (a different chain or position of the functional group).

items.q: What is the functional group of the alkanes?
items.e: The functional group decides the chemical reactions of the series.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of ethane?
items.e: Ethane has 2 carbon atoms (eth-). Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

items.q: Which compound has the formula C₅H₁₂?
items.e: Count the carbon atoms (5: pent-) and look at the functional group.

items.q: How many structural isomers are there of propanol, C₃H₇OH (alcohols only)?
items.e: Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (a different chain or position of the functional group).

items.e: Meth 1, eth 2, prop 3, but 4, pent 5, hex 6.

items.q: How many structural isomers are there of hexane, C₆H₁₄?
items.e: Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (a different chain or position of the functional group).

items.q: Which compound has the formula C₄H₈?
items.e: Count the carbon atoms (4: but-) and look at the functional group.

items.q: What is the formula of propane?
items.e: Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of butane?
items.e: Butane has 4 carbon atoms (but-). Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

items.q: What is the general formula of the alcohols?
items.e: Each member differs from the next by CH₂.

items.q: What is the general formula of the alkenes?
items.e: Each member differs from the next by CH₂.

items.q: Which alkane has the higher boiling point: methane or pentane?
items.e: Longer chains: higher boiling point, more viscous, less flammable.

items.q: What is made in this reaction? ethanol burned in excess oxygen
c: sodium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide
a shorter alkane and an alkene
items.e: Ethanol burned in excess oxygen: carbon dioxide and water.

items.q: What is made in this reaction? ethanoic acid + ethanol (concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, warmed)
c: 1,2-dibromoethane; the orange bromine water is decolourised
items.e: Ethanoic acid + ethanol (concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, warmed): ethyl ethanoate and water.

items.q: What is made in this reaction? methane + chlorine in ultraviolet light
c: a shorter alkane and an alkene
1,2-dibromoethane; the orange bromine water is decolourised
items.e: Methane + chlorine in ultraviolet light: chloromethane and hydrogen chloride.

items.q: Which alkane is more viscous: methane or pentane?
items.e: Longer chains: higher boiling point, more viscous, less flammable.

items.q: What is made in this reaction? ethene + bromine (aqueous)
c: sodium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide
1,2-dibromoethane; the orange bromine water is decolourised
items.e: Ethene + bromine (aqueous): 1,2-dibromoethane; the orange bromine water is decolourised.

items.q: Which alkane has the higher boiling point: butane or pentane?
items.e: Longer chains: higher boiling point, more viscous, less flammable.

items.q: Which alkane has the higher boiling point: methane or hexane?
items.e: Longer chains: higher boiling point, more viscous, less flammable.

items.q: Which reaction gives this result? “ethane”
c: ethanoic acid + ethanol (concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, warmed)
items.e: Ethene + hydrogen (nickel catalyst, about 200 °C): ethane.

items.q: Which alkane is more viscous: ethane or butane?
items.e: Longer chains: higher boiling point, more viscous, less flammable.

items.q: Bromine water is shaken with C₂H₆. What do you see?
c: It turns from orange to colourless.
items.e: Alkenes decolourise bromine water; alkanes do not.

items.q: Which reaction gives this result? “carbon dioxide and water”
c: ethanoic acid + ethanol (concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, warmed)
items.e: Ethanol burned in excess oxygen: carbon dioxide and water.

items.q: Bromine water is shaken with C₅H₁₂. What do you see?
c: It turns from orange to colourless.
items.e: Alkenes decolourise bromine water; alkanes do not.

items.q: Which is an example of combustion?
c: ethanol changing to ethanoic acid with acidified potassium manganate(VII)
decane breaking into octane and ethene
items.e: Propane burning in air: combustion.

items.q: What type of reaction is this: ethanoic acid reacting with ethanol?
items.e: Ethanoic acid reacting with ethanol: esterification (condensation).

items.q: Which is an example of addition?
c: methane reacting with chlorine in UV light
decane breaking into octane and ethene
items.e: Ethene reacting with bromine: addition.

items.q: Bromine water is shaken with C₄H₈. What do you see?
c: It turns from orange to colourless.
items.e: Alkenes decolourise bromine water; alkanes do not.

items.q: Is C₂H₄ an alkane or an alkene?
items.e: Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; alkenes CₙH₂ₙ.

items.q: What type of reaction is this: methane reacting with chlorine in UV light?
items.e: Methane reacting with chlorine in UV light: substitution.

items.q: Which is an example of fermentation?
c: glucose changing to ethanol with yeast
methane reacting with chlorine in UV light
items.e: Glucose changing to ethanol with yeast: fermentation.

items.q: Which reaction gives this result? “chloromethane and hydrogen chloride”
c: ethanoic acid + ethanol (concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, warmed)
items.e: Methane + chlorine in ultraviolet light: chloromethane and hydrogen chloride.

items.q: Which ester is made when ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (ethyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: Which ester is made when ethanoic acid reacts with propanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (propyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: Which compound has the formula C₃H₇OH?
items.e: Count the carbon atoms (3: prop-) and look at the functional group.

items.q: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid. What does this mean?
c: It does not react with metals.
It only partly ionises in water.
items.e: Vinegar is a dilute solution of ethanoic acid.

items.q: Which ester is made when butanoic acid reacts with methanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (methyl) and the acid gives the second part (butanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: Which two compounds react to make ethyl methanoate?
items.e: Ethyl- comes from ethanol; -methanoate comes from methanoic acid.

items.q: Why are alkanes described as saturated?
c: They contain only C–C single bonds.
items.e: No more atoms can be added.

items.q: Which reaction gives this result? “ethyl ethanoate and water”
c: ethanoic acid + ethanol (concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, warmed)
items.e: Ethanoic acid + ethanol (concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, warmed): ethyl ethanoate and water.

items.q: How does the boiling point change as alkanes get longer?
items.e: Larger molecules have stronger forces of attraction between them.

items.q: Which ester is made when propanoic acid reacts with methanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (methyl) and the acid gives the second part (propanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: Which compound has the formula C₂H₅COOH?
items.e: Count the carbon atoms (3: prop-) and look at the functional group.

items.q: What is made in this reaction? ethene + steam (phosphoric(V) acid catalyst, 300 °C, 60 atm)
c: ethanoic acid; the purple solution turns colourless
1,2-dibromoethane; the orange bromine water is decolourised
items.e: Ethene + steam (phosphoric(V) acid catalyst, 300 °C, 60 atm): ethanol.

items.q: Which ester is made when ethanoic acid reacts with methanol?
items.e: The alcohol gives the first part (methyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). Water is also made.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of butanol?
items.e: Butanol has 4 carbon atoms (but-). Alcohols are CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH.

items.q: How can you tell an alkene from an alkane?
c: Add bromine water: the alkene decolourises it, the alkane does not.
Add limewater: the alkene turns it milky.
items.e: The C=C bond reacts by addition.

items.q: Which reaction gives this result? “sodium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide”
c: ethanoic acid + ethanol (concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, warmed)
items.e: Ethanoic acid + sodium carbonate: sodium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of propanol?
items.e: Propanol has 3 carbon atoms (prop-). Alcohols are CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH.

items.q: Why is hydrogenation of vegetable oils used to make margarine?
c: It makes the oil a liquid.
It adds water to the oil.
Adding hydrogen to C=C bonds makes the oil more saturated, so it becomes a solid at room temperature.
items.e: Nickel is the catalyst.

items.q: What is the molecular formula of ethanol?
items.e: Ethanol has 2 carbon atoms (eth-). Alcohols are CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH.

items.q: Which addition polymer is made from the monomer phenylethene (styrene)?
items.e: Put “poly” and brackets around the monomer name.

items.q: What type of reaction is this: ethene molecules joining to make poly(ethene)?
items.e: Ethene molecules joining to make poly(ethene): addition polymerisation.

items.q: What type of reaction is this: propane burning in air?
items.e: Propane burning in air: combustion.

items.q: Which monomer, tetrafluoroethene, is used to make an addition polymer? Choose its formula.
items.e: Every addition monomer has a C=C double bond.

items.q: Which is an example of addition (hydrogenation)?
c: ethene reacting with hydrogen to make ethane
methane reacting with chlorine in UV light
items.e: Ethene reacting with hydrogen to make ethane: addition (hydrogenation).

items.q: Which polymer is used for plastic bags and cling film?
items.e: Poly(ethene): plastic bags and cling film.

items.q: Which polymer is used for ropes and food containers?
items.e: Poly(propene): ropes and food containers.

items.q: Nylon and PET are condensation polymers. What else forms when they are made?
items.e: Monomers with two functional groups join and lose a small molecule each time.

items.q: Which polymer is used for packaging and disposable cups?
items.e: Poly(phenylethene) (polystyrene): packaging and disposable cups.

items.q: Which addition polymer is made from the monomer chloroethene?
items.e: Put “poly” and brackets around the monomer name.

items.q: What is a problem with burning plastic waste?
c: It can release toxic gases such as hydrogen chloride from PVC, and carbon dioxide.
It uses up nitrogen in the air.
items.e: Incinerators need gas cleaning.

items.q: Which polymer is used for non-stick coatings on pans?
items.e: Poly(tetrafluoroethene) (PTFE): non-stick coatings on pans.

items.q: What is the monomer of poly(chloroethene) (PVC)?
items.e: Remove “poly” and the brackets to find the monomer.

items.q: Which is an advantage of recycling plastics?
c: It saves crude oil and reduces plastic waste.
Every plastic can be recycled many times without change.
It uses no energy at all.
items.e: Plastics must first be sorted by type.

items.q: What is the monomer of poly(phenylethene) (polystyrene)?
items.e: Remove “poly” and the brackets to find the monomer.

items.q: Which pair of compounds are isomers?
items.e: Both are C₄H₁₀.

items.q: What type of reaction is this: glucose changing to ethanol with yeast?
items.e: Glucose changing to ethanol with yeast: fermentation.

items.q: Why do plastics cause pollution when thrown away?
c: They are made from renewable plants.
Most are non-biodegradable, so they stay in landfills and the sea for a very long time.
items.e: Plastic waste harms marine life.

items.q: A compound C₃H₆ decolourises bromine water. What is it?
items.e: C₃H₆ fits CₙH₂ₙ, the alkenes.

items.q: Which is an example of esterification (condensation)?
c: ethanol changing to ethanoic acid with acidified potassium manganate(VII)
making nylon from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid
items.e: Ethanoic acid reacting with ethanol: esterification (condensation).
